new_bounded_questions.text: The explicit snapshot-delete command reports a preview and returns before DeleteManifest unless --delete is set. Confirmed snapshot-ID, root-object-ID and source-wide selections use the shared deletion gate; this does not cover automated maintenance.

The full-sync conflict dialog offers upload, download and cancellation with cancellation as that dialog's default. Dedicated full-upload/full-download confirmation paths also exist; the full-download worker calls create_backup_now before closing for replacement. This proves code paths, not a successful or media-complete backup.

The undo manager stores a bounded in-memory queue, truncates old steps and clears undo/redo when a step begins without an undoable operation. Undo therefore is not a durable or universal recovery archive.

Desktop empty-trash displays a permanent-deletion confirmation and calls the trash deletion service only when accepted. The service invokes note/folder deletion; this is not evidence that history or synchronized copies can recover a permanent deletion.

Trash restoration clears deleted_time and restores the parent when available. Missing/deleted parents use either an explicitly requested restore folder or an empty parent ID, unless a target folder is supplied; folder restoration recurses into children.

Automatic trash deletion exits when its enable setting is false, reads an age setting, logs selected items and excludes share-read-only items. It auto-deletes folders only when empty. Inspected setup schedules periodic processing; default setting values and cross-device consequences were not established here.

The pinned trash path stages undo data before setting deletion state. Selected-item restoration runs transactionally, clears deletion state and includes applicable child notes/attachments or subcollections. This is source evidence of intended recovery paths, not a populated-library recovery run.

locators: // Record undo data before modifying state

new_bounded_questions.text: Manual empty-trash asks for confirmation including an irreversible-action message, erases deleted objects and clears undo history. Separately, the item service can purge aged trash from an idle timer using a preference; the manual dialog must not be generalized to all purges or to an observed default retention value.
